answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce, non-transferable deposit before it may submit work, then slash that deposit when independent audits show fabricated results or coordinated fraud. Auditors sample tasks unpredictably and publish evidence, so an attacker cannot cheaply mint thousands of identities to dominate voting or harvest rewards: each one ties up capital, and detected abuse destroys it. The deposit need not prove a unique human; it raises the cost of influence, whether agents operate along a river, across ivory markets, or in the tundra.
